focus: Dropout as described in the introduction: randomly omitting hidden units during training and halving outgoing weights at test time (the 'mean network'). Explain why scaling by the retention probability makes the test-time output equal to the expected training-time output for a single linear unit. Use a small layer of hidden activations and weights the learner can edit, a slider for the retention probability p, and a seed-controlled set of sampled dropout masks. Show individual masked outputs, their running average over many masks, and the mean-network output. Guide the learner through p = 1 (no dropout) and a small p. Check that the mean-network output equals p times the full sum and that the average over all 2^n masks equals it exactly.
audience: engineering undergraduate who knows weighted sums and expected values
